```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

source("_common.R")

# Data flow rule: pages read_rds() only, never call an API. This deck reads the
# same frames summary.qmd reads and computes every number inline, so the slides
# can't drift from the site. Helpers below are the subset of summary.qmd's setup
# that this deck uses; if a definition changes there, change it here too.
stock <- read_rds("data/acs_stock.rds")
demo <- read_rds("data/acs_demographics.rds")
pep <- read_rds("data/pep_migration.rds")
market <- read_rds("data/acs_market.rds")
burden <- read_rds("data/acs_burden.rds")
P <- read_rds("data/pums_profiles.rds")
evict <- read_rds("data/evict.rds")
hmda <- read_rds("data/hmda.rds")
audit <- read_rds("data/summary_audit.rds")

first_yr <- min(demo$population$year)
latest_yr <- max(demo$population$year)

n_fmt <- function(x) scales::label_comma()(x)
p_fmt <- function(x, accuracy = 0.1) scales::label_percent(accuracy = accuracy)(x)
p0 <- function(x) scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1)(x)
round_to <- function(x, k = 1000) n_fmt(round(x / k) * k)
au <- function(key, col = "moe_text") audit |> filter(key == .env$key) |> pull(all_of(col))

# ---- Demographics ----
pop_at <- function(g, yr = latest_yr) {
  demo$population |> filter(geoid == g, year == yr) |> pull(estimate)
}
pop_growth <- function(g) pop_at(g) / pop_at(g, first_yr) - 1

era2 <- levels(pep$era$era)[2]
era_at <- function(g, e, col) pep$era |> filter(geoid == g, era == e) |> pull({{ col }})

age_share <- function(g, grp, yr = latest_yr) {
  demo$age_sex |> filter(geoid == g, year == yr, age_group == grp) |> pull(share) |> sum()
}
inc <- function(g, yr, col = estimate_real) {
  demo$median_income |> filter(geoid == g, year == yr) |> pull({{ col }})
}
inc_real_growth <- function(g) inc(g, latest_yr) / inc(g, first_yr) - 1
# Renter-occupied median household income (B25119): the comparison for would-be buyers.
inc_renter <- function(g, yr, col = estimate_real) {
  demo$median_income_renter |> filter(geoid == g, year == yr) |> pull({{ col }})
}
inc_renter_real_growth <- function(g) inc_renter(g, latest_yr) / inc_renter(g, first_yr) - 1

# ---- Inventory ----
struct_share <- function(g, s) {
  stock$structure_type |> filter(geoid == g, year == latest_yr, structure == s) |> pull(share)
}

# ---- Market ----
med <- function(frame, g, yr, col = estimate_real) {
  frame |> filter(geoid == g, year == yr) |> pull({{ col }})
}
real_chg <- function(frame, g) med(frame, g, latest_yr) / med(frame, g, first_yr) - 1
pti <- function(g, yr) med(market$median_value, g, yr, estimate) / inc_renter(g, yr, estimate)
b30 <- function(g, ten, yr = latest_yr) {
  burden |>
    filter(geoid == g, year == yr, tenure == ten, burden %in% c("Cost-burdened", "Severely cost-burdened")) |>
    pull(share) |>
    sum()
}

# ---- Evictions and lending (core three) ----
ev_sum <- function(g, col) evict$summary |> filter(geoid == g) |> pull(all_of(col))
hm_last <- max(hmda$rates$activity_year)
hm_race <- function(grp, yrs = (hm_last - 3):hm_last) {
  hmda$by_race |>
    filter(race_ethnicity == grp, activity_year %in% yrs) |>
    summarise(rate = sum(denied) / sum(decided_apps)) |>
    pull(rate)
}

# ---- Income bands (PUMS, core three) ----
ami5_lv <- P$levels$ami5
le80 <- function(ten, geo = "Core three") {
  P$le80 |> filter(unit == "Households", .data$geo == .env$geo, .data$tenure == .env$ten) |> pull(est)
}
pr <- function(tp, cat, band, ten) {
  P$profile |>
    filter(topic == tp, category == cat, .data$ami5 == .env$band, .data$tenure == .env$ten) |>
    pull(est)
}
pbsev <- function(band, ten) pr("Cost burden", "Severely cost-burdened (50%+)", band, ten)

hh_count <- function(bands, ten) {
  P$band_counts |>
    filter(unit == "Households", ami5 %in% bands, tenure == ten) |>
    pull(est) |>
    sum()
}
renters_le80 <- hh_count(ami5_lv[1:3], "Renter")
# 65+ households are counted directly from the PUMS records (P$seniors), with
# replicate-weight SEs; n_obs is the unweighted record count.
sen_row <- P$seniors |> filter(unit == "Households", ami5 == "50% AMI or less", tenure == "Renter")
senior_renters_le50 <- sen_row$est
senior_renters_n <- sen_row$n_obs

low_renter <- P$dist5 |>
  filter(unit == "Households", tenure == "Renter", measure == "count", geo != "Core three", band %in% ami5_lv[1:3]) |>
  summarise(n = sum(est), .by = geo) |>
  mutate(share = n / sum(n))
low_renter_city <- low_renter |> filter(geo == "Richmond city") |> pull(share)

# Shared chart bits: blue/orange emphasis, wrapped x labels, slide-sized text.
col_cool <- rva_brand[["blue"]]
col_warm <- rva_brand[["orange"]]
span <- function(text, color) paste0("<b style='color:", color, "'>", text, "</b>")
```

## The region is growing, and migration is doing the work

:::: columns
::: {.column width="38%"}
::: stat
[`r p_fmt(pop_growth("rr17"))`]{.num} [population growth, 17-locality region, `r first_yr` to `r latest_yr` windows]{.lbl}
:::

::: stat
[`r n_fmt(pop_at("rr17"))`]{.num} [people live in the region today]{.lbl}
:::

::: {.stat .warm}
[`r p0(era_at("rr17", era2, mig_share_of_growth))`]{.num} [of regional growth, `r era2`, comes from new people moving into the region]{.lbl}
:::
:::

::: {.column width="62%"}
```{r}
#| label: chart-growth
#| fig-width: 7.4
#| fig-asp: 0.72
#| fig-alt: "Bar chart of population growth between the earlier and latest ACS windows for Richmond city, Henrico, Chesterfield, the four-locality expansion ring and the full region. Chesterfield and the expansion ring grew fastest."

grow_lbl <- c(
  "51760" = "Richmond city", "51087" = "Henrico", "51041" = "Chesterfield",
  "secondary4" = "Expansion ring", "rr17" = "Region"
)
grow <- tibble(
  geoid = names(grow_lbl),
  place = factor(grow_lbl, levels = grow_lbl),
  growth = map_dbl(names(grow_lbl), pop_growth)
)

ggplot(grow, aes(place, growth, fill = place == "Region")) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = p_fmt(growth)), vjust = -0.4, fontface = "bold", size = 7, color = rva_ink[["primary"]]) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = col_warm, "FALSE" = col_cool)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = \(x) str_wrap(x, 9)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.14))) +
  labs(
    subtitle = paste0("Population growth, ", first_yr, " to ", latest_yr, " ACS 5-year windows"),
    caption = acs_cap("B01001")
  ) +
  theme_rva(20) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14))
```
:::
::::

::: notes
This is context, not the argument. Population is up across the region and more of that growth now depends on people moving in, which is why housing supply and cost matter to the region's future. Chesterfield and the expansion ring grew fastest. Richmond city has shifted toward international in-migration.
:::

## About `r round_to(renters_le80)` renter households earn 80% of AMI or less

:::: columns
::: {.column width="38%"}
::: stat
[`r round_to(renters_le80)`]{.num} [City and surrounding county renter households at or below 80% of area median income (AMI): `r p0(le80("Renter"))` of renters]{.lbl}
:::

::: {.stat .warm}
[`r p0(pbsev(ami5_lv[1], "Renter"))`]{.num} [of renters at 30% of AMI or less pay half or more of income on housing]{.lbl}
:::
:::

::: {.column width="62%"}
```{r}
#| label: chart-burden-band
#| fig-width: 7.4
#| fig-asp: 0.72
#| fig-alt: "Stacked bar chart of core-three renters by income band showing the share paying 30 to 49 percent and 50 percent or more of income on housing. The burden is highest in the lowest-income bands and falls steeply above 80 percent of area median income."

bb <- P$profile |>
  filter(topic == "Cost burden", unit == "Households", tenure == "Renter",
         category != "Not cost-burdened", ami5 %in% ami5_lv) |>
  mutate(
    ami5 = factor(ami5, levels = ami5_lv),
    category = factor(category, levels = c("Cost-burdened (30-49%)", "Severely cost-burdened (50%+)"))
  )
bb_tot <- bb |> summarise(total = sum(est), .by = ami5)

ggplot(bb, aes(ami5, est, fill = category)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(
    data = bb_tot, aes(ami5, total, label = p0(total)), inherit.aes = FALSE,
    vjust = -0.4, fontface = "bold", size = 6.5, color = rva_ink[["primary"]]
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Cost-burdened (30-49%)" = col_cool, "Severely cost-burdened (50%+)" = col_warm)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = \(x) str_wrap(x, 8)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(
    subtitle = paste0("Core three renters paying 30%+ of income on housing<br>", span("50%+", col_warm), " and ", span("30-49%", col_cool), ", by income band"),
    caption = pums_cap()
  ) +
  theme_rva(20) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14))
```
:::
::::

::: notes
AMI is area median income, using HUD limits for the Richmond area. The core three are Richmond city, Henrico and Chesterfield. Need is deepest at the bottom: most of the lowest-income renters pay half or more of income on housing. The top band is a small sample, so don't quote it.
:::

## Home values rose far faster than renter incomes

:::: columns
::: {.column width="38%"}
::: {.stat .warm}
[`r p0(b30("rr17", "Renter"))`]{.num} [of renter households pay 30% or more of income on housing (`r p0(b30("rr17", "Renter", first_yr))` in the `r first_yr` window)]{.lbl}
:::

::: stat
[`r p0(b30("rr17", "Owner"))`]{.num} [of owners pay 30% or more, down from `r p0(b30("rr17", "Owner", first_yr))`]{.lbl}
:::
:::

::: {.column width="62%"}
```{r}
#| label: chart-price-income
#| fig-width: 7.4
#| fig-asp: 0.72
#| fig-alt: "Bar chart of inflation-adjusted change in Richmond MSA medians between the earlier and latest ACS windows. Median home value rose far more than median renter household income and median gross rent."

chg <- tibble(
  measure = factor(
    c("Median renter household income", "Median gross rent", "Median home value"),
    levels = c("Median renter household income", "Median gross rent", "Median home value")
  ),
  change = c(inc_renter_real_growth("40060"), real_chg(market$median_rent, "40060"), real_chg(market$median_value, "40060"))
)

ggplot(chg, aes(measure, change, fill = measure)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = p0(change)), vjust = -0.4, fontface = "bold", size = 7, color = rva_ink[["primary"]]) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(col_cool, col_cool, col_warm)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = \(x) str_wrap(x, 12)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(
    subtitle = paste0("Richmond MSA, change after inflation,<br>", first_yr, " to ", latest_yr, " ACS 5-year windows"),
    caption = acs_cap("B25119, B25064, B25077")
  ) +
  theme_rva(20)
```
:::
::::

::: notes
Home value is the stronger finding: its rise is outside the margins of error. Rent and renter-income changes are within each other's margins of error, so do not say rent grew faster than renter income. Renter burden is essentially unchanged region-wide; owner burden fell. Dollar changes are adjusted with national CPI-U.
:::

## Eviction filings are nearly back to pre-pandemic levels

:::: columns
::: {.column width="34%"}
::: stat
[`r p0(-ev_sum("bhc3", "latest12_vs_pre"))`]{.num} [below the 2016-19 monthly average, over the latest 12 months]{.lbl}
:::

::: {.stat .warm}
[about `r round_to(ev_sum("bhc3", "latest12_mean"), 100)`]{.num} [filings a month in the core three]{.lbl}
:::

::: kicker
Filings are landlord court requests, not completed evictions. The 2020-21 low reflects pandemic moratoria and rental assistance.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r}
#| label: chart-evictions
#| fig-width: 7.8
#| fig-asp: 0.7
#| fig-alt: "Column chart of annual eviction filings in the core three localities. Filings were around seven thousand to eight thousand a year before 2020, fell sharply in 2020 and 2021, and have recovered in later years."

ev_plot <- evict$annual |> filter(geoid == "bhc3", complete_year)
pre_mean <- ev_plot |> filter(year < 2020) |> summarise(m = mean(filings)) |> pull(m)

ggplot(ev_plot, aes(factor(year), filings)) +
  geom_col(fill = col_cool, width = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = pre_mean, linetype = "dashed", color = rva_ink[["muted"]]) +
  annotate("text", x = "2021", y = pre_mean, label = "2016-19 average", vjust = -0.6, size = 5.5, color = rva_ink[["muted"]]) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n_fmt(filings)), vjust = -0.4, size = 5, color = rva_ink[["primary"]]) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(
    subtitle = "Core three, eviction filings per year",
    caption = paste0(eviction_cap(), " Complete years only.")
  ) +
  theme_rva(20)
```
:::
::::

::: notes
Lead with the trend against the pre-2020 baseline, not a count of displaced households. The provider's own "percent of historical average" has no documented definition, so use the count-based comparison to the 2016-19 monthly mean. Covers Richmond city, Henrico and Chesterfield only.
:::

## The 65-and-over share is rising across the region

:::: columns
::: {.column width="34%"}
::: stat
[about `r round_to(senior_renters_le50, 500)`]{.num} [core-three renter households at or below 50% of AMI with a householder 65 or over]{.lbl}
:::

::: {.stat .warm}
[`r p0(age_share("secondary4", "65 and over"))`]{.num} [of expansion-ring residents are 65 or over, the oldest part of the region]{.lbl}
:::

::: kicker
The senior count is a PUMS survey estimate from `r n_fmt(senior_renters_n)` sample households. Quote it as "about".
:::
:::

::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r}
#| label: chart-seniors
#| fig-width: 7.8
#| fig-asp: 0.7
#| fig-alt: "Grouped column chart of the share of residents aged 65 and over in Richmond city, Henrico, Chesterfield, the expansion ring and the full region in the earlier and latest ACS windows. The share rose everywhere and is highest in the expansion ring."

geo_lbl <- c(
  "51760" = "Richmond city", "51087" = "Henrico", "51041" = "Chesterfield",
  "secondary4" = "Expansion ring", "rr17" = "Region"
)
age_plot <- expand_grid(geoid = names(geo_lbl), year = c(first_yr, latest_yr)) |>
  mutate(
    share = map2_dbl(geoid, year, \(g, y) age_share(g, "65 and over", y)),
    place = factor(geo_lbl[geoid], levels = geo_lbl),
    year = factor(year)
  )
yr_cols <- setNames(c(rva_seq[[3]], rva_seq[[6]]), c(first_yr, latest_yr))

ggplot(age_plot, aes(place, share, fill = year)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = p0(share)), position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    vjust = -0.4, size = 5, color = rva_ink[["primary"]]
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = yr_cols) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = \(x) str_wrap(x, 10)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(
    subtitle = paste0("Share of residents 65 and over, ", span(first_yr, yr_cols[[1]]), " and ", span(latest_yr, yr_cols[[2]]), " windows"),
    caption = acs_cap("B01001")
  ) +
  theme_rva(20)
```
:::
::::

::: notes
BHC operates 8 senior affordable properties. The group they serve is growing as a share of the region. Older owners are exposed too: about half of owners at or below 30% of AMI (`r p0(pr("Householder age", "65 and over", ami5_lv[1], "Owner"))`) are 65 or over. The expansion ring also had more deaths than births, so its growth depends on in-migration. Senior counts are weighted PUMS estimates, so round to the nearest 500.
:::

## Homes cost more relative to income, and credit access is uneven

:::: columns
::: {.column width="38%"}
::: {.stat .warm}
[`r sprintf("%.1f", pti("40060", first_yr))` to `r sprintf("%.1f", pti("40060", latest_yr))`]{.num} [typical home value as a multiple of typical renter household income, Richmond MSA]{.lbl}
:::

::: stat
[`r sprintf("%.1f", hm_race("Black") / hm_race("White, non-Hispanic"))`x]{.num} [Black applicants were denied home-purchase loans this many times as often as non-Hispanic White applicants]{.lbl}
:::
:::

::: {.column width="62%"}
```{r}
#| label: chart-denial
#| fig-width: 7.4
#| fig-asp: 0.72
#| fig-alt: "Bar chart of pooled home-purchase denial rates in the core three over the last four years. Black and Hispanic or Latino applicants were denied more often than Asian and non-Hispanic White applicants."

den_groups <- c("Black", "Hispanic or Latino", "Asian", "White, non-Hispanic")
den <- tibble(group = den_groups, rate = map_dbl(den_groups, hm_race)) |>
  mutate(
    group = factor(group, levels = den_groups),
    emph = group %in% c("Black", "Hispanic or Latino")
  )

ggplot(den, aes(group, rate, fill = emph)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = p_fmt(rate)), vjust = -0.4, fontface = "bold", size = 7, color = rva_ink[["primary"]]) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = col_warm, "FALSE" = col_cool)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = \(x) str_wrap(x, 11)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.14))) +
  labs(
    subtitle = paste0("Home-purchase denial rate, core three,<br>", hm_last - 3, "-", hm_last, " pooled"),
    caption = "**Source:** FFIEC/CFPB HMDA. Denied / (originated + approved-not-accepted + denied); one- to four-unit principal residences."
  ) +
  theme_rva(20)
```
:::
::::

::: notes
Value-to-income uses every owner's own estimate of value, so it understates the cost of buying today. The denial rates are loan records, not a sample, and exclude withdrawn and incomplete applications. Some applications have no race or ethnicity recorded. Don't describe denial reasons as home-purchase reasons; most denials in the lending data are refinance, cash-out and home-improvement loans.
:::

## Low-income renters aren't just in the city

:::: columns
::: {.column width="62%"}
```{r}
#| label: chart-low-renters
#| fig-width: 7.4
#| fig-asp: 0.72
#| fig-alt: "Bar chart of renter households at or below 80 percent of area median income in Henrico, Chesterfield and Richmond city, with each locality's share of the core-three total."

lr <- low_renter |>
  mutate(
    geo = fct_reorder(geo, n, .desc = TRUE),
    lab = paste0(round_to(n, 500), "\n(", p0(share), ")")
  )

ggplot(lr, aes(geo, n)) +
  geom_col(fill = col_cool, width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = lab), vjust = -0.3, fontface = "bold", size = 6.5, lineheight = 0.95, color = rva_ink[["primary"]]) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.25))) +
  labs(
    subtitle = "Renter households at or below 80% of AMI,<br>and share of the core-three total",
    caption = pums_cap()
  ) +
  theme_rva(20)
```
:::

::: {.column width="38%"}
::: stat
[`r p0(1 - low_renter_city)`]{.num} [of lower-income renter households live in Henrico or Chesterfield, not Richmond city]{.lbl}
:::

::: stat
[`r p0(struct_share("51760", "20+ units"))`]{.num} [of Richmond city's housing is in buildings of 20+ units, the only multifamily-heavy core locality]{.lbl}
:::

::: {.stat .warm}
[`r p0(struct_share("bhc3", "Single-family detached"))`]{.num} [of core-three housing is detached single-family homes]{.lbl}
:::
:::
::::

::: notes
Richmond city has the highest share of lower-income households, but most of the lower-income renters live in the suburbs, so mixed-income communities have a role in all three localities. These data speak to income, tenure and structure type; they do not measure demand for retail or commercial space, which needs separate evidence. Housing is old in the city and vacancy is tight in the suburbs, which limits affordable options without new construction.
:::

Status as shown on the Virginia Legislative Information System (LIS) on November 12, 2026, before the session opens. Bill text can change in committee.

::: notes
Nine bills already on LIS. Most were carried over from the 2026 session. HB183 passed the House 96 to 2 in February 2026 and is in Senate Finance and Appropriations; SB717 passed the Senate and is in House Counties, Cities and Towns. The next slides group them by theme and add the proposals that are not filed yet.
:::

## Tenants: three bills on mold, fees and deposits

::: icon-list
- []{.ico .ico-droplet}**[HB79](https://lis.virginia.gov/bill-details/20271/HB79), mold.** Lets tenants sue for damages, including punitive damages and attorney fees, when mold results solely from a landlord's gross negligence or willful misconduct. Requires temporary vacating for remediation when a physician certifies a health risk.
- []{.ico .ico-receipt}**[HB1409](https://lis.virginia.gov/bill-details/20271/HB1409), rental agreement fees.** Bars agreements that charge tenants for building maintenance, pest control, trash, common-area utilities or security, or for internet and cable above the landlord's cost.
- []{.ico .ico-key}**[SB349](https://lis.virginia.gov/bill-details/20271/SB349), pre-tenancy fees.** Limits landlords to defined pre-tenancy fees, requires written notice of them before collecting anything, and limits how security and pet deposits can be applied.
:::

::: notes
All three amend the Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act. HB79 and HB1409 were continued to 2027 in House General Laws, and in 2026 a subcommittee recommended continuing each to 2028, so watch whether either gets a hearing. These are summaries from LIS, not legal analysis.
:::

## Land use: five bills on approvals and public land

::: icon-list
- []{.ico .ico-clock}**[HB419](https://lis.virginia.gov/bill-details/20271/HB419), approval deadlines.** Every locality must approve, approve with conditions, or deny a residential rezoning or development application within 12 months.
- []{.ico .ico-pin}**[SB717](https://lis.virginia.gov/bill-details/20271/SB717), transit-oriented overlays.** Requires six stories and 30 units per acre by right near major transit stops, ministerial approval, effective September 2027 with a 2030 sunset. Passed the Senate in 2026.
- []{.ico .ico-landmark}**[HB143](https://lis.virginia.gov/bill-details/20271/HB143), surplus property.** Offers suitable state surplus land to affordable housing developers for at least 90 days, with a 30-year affordability covenant; localities inventory their own land.
- []{.ico .ico-building}**[HB1376](https://lis.virginia.gov/bill-details/20271/HB1376), redevelopment fund.** Removes the $500,000 cap and the 100% local match on the Urban Public-Private Partnership Redevelopment Fund.
- []{.ico .ico-home}**[HB464](https://lis.virginia.gov/bill-details/20271/HB464), accessory dwelling units.** Directs the state housing department to publish a construction guide with local rules and model designs.
:::

::: notes
SB717 is the most far-reaching. As passed by the Senate it covers certain localities, allows some areas to be excluded, and ends September 1, 2030. HB419 was continued in House Counties, Cities and Towns, with a subcommittee recommending continuing it to 2028.
:::

## Homeownership: bigger savings accounts, revised tax credit

::: icon-list
- []{.ico .ico-wallet}**[HB183](https://lis.virginia.gov/bill-details/20271/HB183), savings plan (filed).** Adds townhouses, raises the principal limit from $50,000 to $100,000 and the retained-balance limit from $150,000 to $200,000, and defines first-time buyer. Passed the House 96 to 2.
- []{.ico .ico-file}**Housing Opportunity Tax Credit (expected).** Add a certificated-credit option and shorten the credit period from 10 years to five to raise credit value.
- []{.ico .ico-key}**Acquisition Fund pilot (budget request).** A three-year revolving loan program run by the state housing department to buy and preserve units at affordable rates, for localities with a right-of-first-refusal ordinance that match state dollars.
:::

::: notes
HB183 is a savings-account bill; it helps households that can already save, so pair it with the renter-income numbers earlier in the deck. The tax credit change and the acquisition pilot are not filed yet, and the pilot's dollar amount is not set.
:::

## Not yet filed: zoning and parking bills

::: icon-list
- []{.ico .ico-home}**Starter and Silver Homes.** Limit minimum lot sizes, setbacks and lot dimensions in new subdivisions to allow smaller homes.
- []{.ico .ico-users}**Co-living.** Remove arbitrary limits on who can live together, with health and safety standards kept.
- []{.ico .ico-pin}**Transit-oriented development.** Revisit targeted upzoning near transit.
- []{.ico .ico-file}**Faith in Housing fixes.** Clarify the sunset, industrial-zoning, height and historic-preservation provisions.
- []{.ico .ico-parking}**Parking reform.** Widen "designated areas" and transit stops, and cap commercial parking at two spaces per 1,000 square feet.
- []{.ico .ico-bike}**Multi-modal parking.** Let developers swap required car spaces for bicycle spaces one to one.
:::

::: notes
None of these are on LIS yet, so wording and patrons are not settled. Check LIS for filed bill numbers once pre-filing opens.
:::

## Not yet filed: budget requests and right to rest

::: icon-list
- []{.ico .ico-users}**5,000 Families pilot.** Three-year pilot of ongoing rental assistance for low-income families with children.
- []{.ico .ico-wallet}**Virginia Housing Trust Fund.** Increase the biennial total to expand the supply of homes and housing stability.
- []{.ico .ico-home}**Homeless Solutions Program.** More program funding plus a set-aside for provider capacity.
- []{.ico .ico-key}**State Rental Assistance Program.** $2.4 million a year and one staff position to restore vouchers for people with disabilities.
- []{.ico .ico-bed}**Right to rest.** Bar localities from arresting or fining people for sleeping or resting in public places where they do not block access or create a hazard.
:::

::: notes
Dollar amounts for most budget items depend on the Governor's budget and the Housing Trust Fund workgroup report, so none are shown except the agency-requested rental assistance figure.
:::

## Six numbers you can quote

```{r}
#| label: quotables

quotes <- tribble(
  ~Figure, ~Value, ~`Margin of error (90%)`, ~Where, ~Note,
  "Renter households at or below 80% of AMI",
    paste0("about ", round_to(renters_le80), " (", p0(le80("Renter")), " of renters)"),
    au("renters_le80"), "Core three", "Say \"about\"",
  "Renters at or below 30% of AMI paying half or more of income on housing",
    p0(pbsev(ami5_lv[1], "Renter")), au("renter_le30_sev"), "Core three", "",
  "Renter households paying 30%+ of income on housing",
    p0(b30("rr17", "Renter")), au("renter_b30_2024"), "17-locality region", "Not improved since 2014",
  "Senior renter households at or below 50% of AMI",
    paste0("about ", round_to(senior_renters_le50, 500)), au("senior_renters_le50"), "Core three", "Small sample; say \"about\"",
  "Typical home value vs. typical renter household income",
    paste0(sprintf("%.1f", pti("40060", first_yr)), " to ", sprintf("%.1f", pti("40060", latest_yr)), " times"),
    au("pti_2024"), "Richmond MSA", "",
  "Home-purchase denial rate, Black vs. White non-Hispanic applicants",
    paste0(p0(hm_race("Black")), " vs. ", p0(hm_race("White, non-Hispanic"))),
    paste0(au("denial_Black"), " / ", au("denial_White")), "Core three", "Loan records; some lack race data"
)

quotes |> kbl(format = "html", align = "lllll")
```

::: kicker
AMI = area median income. ACS and PUMS figures are the `r latest_yr` 5-year window. Margins of error are published ACS values or PUMS replicate-weight standard errors x 1.645 (see `r/summary_audit.R`).
:::

::: notes
These are the figures with margins of error already worked out. The full table, with the eviction and population figures, is on the Summary page of the site.
:::

## Using these numbers well

::: cautions
- **These are regional figures, not BHC results.** They describe need and market conditions in Richmond city, Henrico and Chesterfield, or the 17-locality region where noted. Pair them with BHC's own program data.
- **Say "at or below 80% of AMI," not "low-income,"** unless you define the term.
- **Round survey counts and say "about."** Household counts by income band are estimates with sampling error.
- **Say home values rose faster than renter incomes.** Check the rent and renter-income margins of error before saying rent outpaced income.
- **Eviction filings are not evictions.** Lead with the trend against the pre-2020 baseline, not a count of displaced households.
- **Bill status changes daily.** The legislation slides are a November 12, 2026 snapshot; check LIS before quoting a bill's status, and treat unfiled proposals as proposals.
:::

::: kicker
Full detail, definitions and sources: the Summary and Data Notes pages of the RVA Sourcebook. Questions?
:::

::: notes
Open the floor for Q&A here. This slide is the one people will want back on screen when they ask how to word something. The data do not measure demand for mixed-use space, and the senior counts rest on `r n_fmt(senior_renters_n)` sample households (margin of error `r au("senior_renters_le50")`).
:::
